comparison: Perfect agreement on eIF2A localization claims (C49-C54, C100-C101). Both evaluations support the cytosolic localization findings and lack of stress-induced changes. Reviewers accepted these findings without challenge, noting consistency with previous work.

Perfect agreement on overexpression experiments (C55, C103). Both evaluations support the finding that eIF2A overexpression does not suppress global translation. Reviewers specifically endorsed this as part of comprehensive negative results contradicting recent claims.

Perfect agreement on ribosome profiling results (C57-C62, C66, C72-C73, C75, C105). Both evaluations strongly support these findings. Reviewers emphasized high precision, reproducibility, and the compelling nature of the minimal changes observed, with comparison to other translation factors strengthening conclusions.

Strong agreement on uORF translation claims (C77-C80, C114-C116). OpenEval R8 covers 7 claims while peer R6 covers 8 claims with substantial overlap. Both evaluations support the negative uORF findings. Reviewers praised the comprehensive approach including direct peptide detection (C83 in peer evaluation).

Strong agreement on validation experiments (C67-C71). Both evaluations support these findings, with peer review also mentioning C106. The lack of validation for most candidates was seen as strengthening rather than weakening the conclusion of minimal eIF2A function.

Partial agreement on global translation measurements. OpenEval R2 focuses on C42-C45, C56 while peer R1 covers C38-C45, C56, spanning both knockout generation and translation assays. Both strongly support these findings with reviewers praising thoroughness and precision.

Partial agreement on knockout generation (C38-C41). OpenEval R1 focuses specifically on knockout validation while peer R1 groups this with global translation measurements. Both evaluations fully support the knockout generation and validation approach.

Partial agreement on stress condition ribosome profiling (C92-C95, C111-C112). OpenEval R11 focuses on tunicamycin ribosome profiling while peer R7 covers broader stress findings including C86-C90, C96-C99. Both strongly support the negative results under stress conditions.

Partial agreement on ISR response claims (C86-C90). OpenEval R10 focuses on ISR measurements while peer R7 covers comprehensive stress findings. Both evaluations support the conclusion that eIF2A is not required for the integrated stress response.

Partial agreement on uORF translation under stress (C96-C99). OpenEval R12 specifically addresses uORF behavior under tunicamycin while peer R7 covers broader stress findings. Both support negative results for eIF2A role in stress-induced uORF translation.

Strong agreement on contextualization with recent literature (C119-C121). OpenEval R15 focuses on literature comparison while peer R9 also includes main conclusion C137. Both evaluations support the consistency with recent findings, with reviewers emphasizing the value of independent confirmation.

Agreement on main conclusion (C6, C137). OpenEval R14 addresses the primary conclusion while peer R9 groups this with literature context. Both strongly support the conclusion that eIF2A is not required for translation initiation, with reviewers describing evidence as compelling.

Agreement on HEK293T cell validation (C81-C82). OpenEval R9 covers broader uORF findings including C83 while peer R8 focuses on cell-type extension. Both evaluations support these experiments as addressing cell-type specificity concerns.

Minimal overlap on SIINFEKL peptide detection (C83). OpenEval R9 includes this as part of comprehensive uORF analysis while peer R6 mentions it in context of uORF translation. Both support this direct measurement approach.

Agreement on alternative initiation factors (C117). Both evaluations support this analysis addressing potential redundancy. OpenEval R13 focuses specifically on this claim while peer R10 also includes C118. Reviewers accepted this as appropriate acknowledgment of limitations.

Agreement on study limitations (C131). OpenEval R16 addresses speculative alternative functions (C125, C127, C131) while peer R11 focuses on cell-type limitations (C130-C131). Both evaluations accept these as appropriately acknowledged limitations.

OpenEval R7 addresses hairpin-AUG luciferase reporters (C74) testing codon-dependent tRNA delivery. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this claim, though it supports the broader negative conclusions.
